title: Orbitronics in Zero-dimensional Graphene Nanoflakes via Electrode Coupling
authors: Washington F. dos Santos, Eudes Gomes da Silva, Denis R. Candido, Alexandre Reily Rocha
abstract: We show that graphene nanoflakes realize a previously unexplored form of orbitronics in which orbital currents emerge in the absence of intrinsic angular momentum of the constituent atoms. Starting with a hexagonal graphene nanoflake, we demonstrate the presence of energy-degenerate eigenstates with opposite non-zero expectation values of the angular momentum. Placing electrodes in an appropriate configuration on the flake couples the reservoirs more strongly to one of the two opposite-angular-momentum states, yielding a chiral current that carries a net orbital angular momentum. The resulting circulating orbital currents generate magnetic fringe fields that are experimentally accessible with spin centers or superconducting quantum interference magnetometers, providing avenues for their experimental realization. Finally, our work establishes a new platform for exploring and studying orbitronics in zero-dimensional systems.
summary: This paper demonstrates that graphene nanoflakes can exhibit 'orbitronics'—circulating orbital currents—even though the carbon atoms lack intrinsic orbital angular momentum. By coupling the flake to electrodes, the system develops a net chiral current carrying orbital angular momentum. This current generates a magnetic field that can be experimentally measured using advanced nanoscale magnetometers.
main_problem: The paper investigates a novel form of 'orbitronics' in zero-dimensional graphene nanoflakes (GNFs), demonstrating orbital currents that arise without intrinsic angular momentum in the constituent atoms.
main_result: By coupling the GNF to external electrodes, the system develops a net chiral circulating current carrying a measurable orbital angular momentum, which generates detectable magnetic fringe fields.
method: The study employs the non-equilibrium Keldysh formalism to calculate current densities and magnetic fields, analyzing the system's response to electrode coupling.
model_or_system: The physical system is a hexagonal graphene nanoflake modeled using a tight-binding approximation based on $p_z$ orbitals, coupled to two semi-infinite leads (electrodes) at the vertices.
key_observables: Orbital Angular Momentum ($\langle \hat{L}_z angle$), chiral current density, and the resulting magnetic fringe field ($B_z$).
important_parameters: The coupling strength to the leads, which is necessary to break symmetry and induce the net OAM current.
main_assumptions: The GNF is modeled solely using $p_z$ orbitals, ensuring zero initial atomic OAM, and the analysis uses the non-equilibrium Keldysh formalism.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate the setup, the dependence of the Density of States (DOS) on coupling, the emergence of chiral current, and the calculated magnetic fringe field $B_z$ detectable by NV centers or SQUID magnetometers.
paper_structure: The work progresses from establishing the theoretical framework for OAM in GNF, calculating the current using Keldysh formalism, demonstrating the necessary symmetry breaking via electrode coupling, and finally predicting the measurable magnetic signature.
why_interesting: The concept of generating macroscopic orbital currents purely through geometric coupling in a zero-dimensional system, detectable via magnetic probes, provides a novel platform for studying orbital degrees of freedom beyond standard charge transport.
